_comment: klt erc supply spec for the tile's routed GDS -- T1 checklist item 11
(power delivery, structural) of docs/design-evidence-tiers.md in
2AMLogic/klayout-tools, approved as klayout-tools#2025 on 2026-09-17.
This spec plus its committed report (layout/logic_tile.erc.json,
regenerated and diff-checked by flow/erc.sh) are the item-11 evidence
artifacts issue #51 asked for. The worked example this file follows is
gf180-drone-fc's layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json.
Run it against the committed routed GDS (flow/erc.sh runs exactly this,
from the repo root, so the report's file/spec fields are repo-relative
and host-independent):
klt erc layout/logic_tile.gds layout/erc-supply-spec.json \
--top logic_tile --format json
--pdk is deliberately NOT passed. It would select klt's own built-in
antenna-ratio table: the antenna verdict is a real check but it is not
item 11's subject (design-evidence-tiers.md: an antenna or floating-gate
finding is a real defect but does not block the item, klayout-tools
#1994), and it would stamp provenance.pdk with the built-in table's
identity rather than the PDK install, so the committed report stays
clearer without it (every antenna verdict in it reads 'unchecked',
which is the honest state of what this run graded).
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- stackup[0] MUST carry role: "gate" (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at poly. active_layer makes gate identification and the
antenna denominator poly n diff instead of raw poly area, keeping
fill-cell poly bars -- real poly with no gate oxide -- out of gates[]
instead of reporting non-physical ratios for them (klayout-tools
docs/cli/erc.md, issue #1979).
- The stackup covers the routing levels this block actually uses, per
issue #51: li1 through met4. The routed DEF carries four NEW met4
segments (and the GDS real licon1/mcon/via1/via2/via3 stacks up to
them via one met3-met4 via per route), while the stream carries zero
met5 (72/20) and zero via4 (71/44) geometry -- so met5 and via4 are
deliberately absent, matching klt erc's own convention that naming an
absent layer is allowed but this spec scopes to what this block draws.
- label_layer is declared ONLY on the two layers the merged GDS
actually carries VPWR/VGND text on: li1.label 67/5 (4 VPWR + 4 VGND,
the standard cells' own li1-level supply pin text) and met1.label
68/5 (196 VPWR + 196 VGND, the klt met1 -followpins row-rail pin
text -- all 392 texts on 68/5 in this stream are supply labels).
met2.label/met3.label carry signal-pin-only text, so declaring them
would add nothing (gf180-drone-fc's spec reasons identically about its
Metal2).
- GDS layer numbers are sky130's own drawn-layer numbers, resolved from
the PDK's libs.tech/klayout/tech/sky130A.lyp AND cross-checked against
klayout-tools' curated sky130 deck layer table (poly.drawing 66/20,
diff.drawing 65/20, li1.drawing 67/20, met1.drawing 68/20,
met2.drawing 69/20, met3.drawing 70/20, met4.drawing 71/20,
licon1.drawing 66/44, mcon.drawing 67/44, via1/via 68/44,
via2 69/44, via3 70/44) -- not copied from another PDK's spec.
- nets[]: VPWR and VGND, both kind: "supply" -- the two nets the
place-and-route report names as the row-rail supply pair
(layout/logic_tile.par.json: power.row_rail.power_net/.ground_net).
kind is what makes a short between the two report as the severe
erc.supply_short rather than the milder erc.multiply_driven_net.
Each must resolve to exactly ONE electrical island:
erc.unconnected_net fires on zero matches AND on more than one, so
zero findings of that rule naming a declared supply is exactly the
one-island-per-supply verdict -- and a split rail is precisely the
no-PDN failure mode this spec exists to detect.
- There is deliberately NO ties[] section here, and that is a recorded
gap, not an oversight. Declaring one on a real routed standard-cell
design collapses the design into one electrical island and reports a
FALSE erc.supply_short -- klayout-tools#2169, reproduced four ways in
gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION F-034. Per docs/cli/erc.md, 'Omitted
entirely -> erc.missing_tie is never computed', so the committed
report's absence of a missing_tie count is an absence of evidence,
not evidence of absence; klt signoff renders a no-ties spec
supply_spec_incomplete for exactly that reason (klayout-tools#2199),
so read item 11's well-tie leg from this spec as NOT computed. The
well-tie evidence that does stand in, named per issue #51: the merged
GDS carries the standard cells' own well/bulk PG pin text -- 201 VPB
labels on nwell.label 64/5 and 201 VNB labels on pwell.label 64/59
-- plus the supply pin labels above. What does NOT stand in, and must
not be read as tie evidence: the place-and-route request inserted no
tapcells (power.tapcell_master: null, power.pdn: false, straps: [])
and the stream carries zero tap.drawing 65/44 geometry, so no drawn
tie exists at all. The split-supply-rail finding this spec measured
in the current committed layout -- VPWR resolves to 7 islands, VGND
to 8, the 15 met1 rails issue #41 names -- is the open PDN work.
